clue.text: There's nothing in sleeping area located by uncomplaining figure

indicators.note: the nothing-letter goes inside the word for the sleeping area

parts.note: a dorm is a dormitory, a shared sleeping room
O is the zero shape, nothing
at means located by or beside, as in 'at the door'

explanation.surface: Someone notices the nought in a dormitory next to a meek person.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who lets everyone walk over them without protest is called a doormat, an idiom.

clue.text: Offer a note supporting academic

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means sitting below the academic word

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A short instruction: give a teacher a written note.
explanation.definitionFit: To donate is to give or present something, a synonym for offer as a verb.

clue.text: Start of tour in old French city largely as scheduled

indicators.note: the opening letter of tour goes into the shortened city
largely means most of it, so the city loses its last letter

parts.note: Nimes is a city in southern France

indicators.note: start of means the first letter of tour

explanation.surface: A tour starts in an ancient French city according to plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' cuts NIMES to NIME; the T of tour goes after its N.
explanation.definitionFit: Being punctual, arriving when expected, is what the phrase means: according to the timetable.

clue.text: Run into bend beyond central area? It's not unduly demanding

indicators.note: beyond means coming after, so the bend piece follows

parts.note: the middle is the central area of something

indicators.note: into means the run letter is placed inside the bend word

parts.note: to bow is to bend
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Jog to the curve past the centre: an easy exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Middlebrow culture is accessible, neither highbrow nor lowbrow, so asks little of its audience.

clue.text: Deliver small rug

definitions.meaning: to deliver a ball, as a bowler or pitcher does, is to hurl it
a small blanket or cover laid over furniture

explanation.surface: Hand over a little mat.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a bowler delivers the ball by hurling it, and a light cover over a sofa is so called.

clue.text: I lift up folds in a sad state

indicators.note: the words fold over on themselves, so the letters of I lift up get rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone raising a load collapses, a sorry sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'folds' looks like the verb of collapsing; it signals the anagram of I LIFT UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pitiful arouses pity because it is wretched, a synonym for being in a sad state.

clue.text: Material in old college guide (with centre displaced)

parts.note: a poly was a polytechnic, a British college type abolished in 1992

indicators.note: the central letter of the word for guide is shifted to a new position

parts.note: to steer is to guide

explanation.surface: Fabric found in a former polytechnic's handbook, with its middle rearranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with centre displaced' moves the middle E of STEER to the front, giving ESTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Polyester is a synthetic fibre used to make fabric, an example of material.

clue.text: Instant sign of credit

definitions.meaning: a moment, as in 'just a second'
a check mark showing something is correct
buying on credit, deferred payment, informally

explanation.surface: A quick acknowledgement that someone deserves recognition.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions joined by 'of'. 'On tick' is British slang for buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Each sense fits the same short word: a moment, a check mark, and informal deferred payment.

clue.text: Untarnished force avoiding regulation

parts.note: F is the physics abbreviation for force
lawless means not keeping to laws or rules

explanation.surface: A police force that is clean because it dodges red tape.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without any defect or blemish is perfect, so it is untarnished.

clue.text: One in suit altered tailoring wanting alternative tweed principally

indicators.note: altered, apt for tailoring, says the remaining letters change their order
wanting means lacking, so these letters are removed from tailoring

parts.note: or introduces an alternative

indicators.note: principally means first, so take the opening letter of tweed

explanation.surface: Someone in a suit has it altered, but the tailoring lacks some tweed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' is a lawsuit, not clothing. 'wanting alternative' drops the word meaning or, and 'altered' rearranges what is left before the tweed initial is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A litigant is a party to a lawsuit, so one in a suit is a legal pun.

clue.text: Eminent name traduced principally in dictionary

indicators.note: the first letter of traduced sits inside the dictionary's abbreviation

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

indicators.note: principally means first of all, so take the opening letter of traduced

explanation.surface: A distinguished person's name is slandered in a dictionary entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Noted people are well known and respected, a synonym for eminent.

clue.text: Unwilling lecturer to face a cut possibly in payment

indicators.note: the built-up piece goes inside the word for payment

parts.note: rent is a regular payment for property

indicators.note: the lecturer letter stands in front of, facing, the rearranged letters
possibly says a cut may be rearranged into another order

explanation.surface: A lecturer is reluctant to confront a cut in pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' is the anagram signal for A CUT; 'to face' puts the lecturer's L in front, and 'in' places the lot inside the payment word.
explanation.definitionFit: Reluctant describes someone holding back from doing something, a synonym for unwilling.

clue.text: Twig, minute, close to potted plant

parts.note: to twig and to tumble both mean to realise or catch on (informal)
minute (my-NEWT) means tiny, wee

indicators.note: close to means the closing letter of potted

explanation.surface: A tiny twig sits next to a potted plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twig' and 'minute' look like a sprig and a unit of time; they are the verb 'realise' and the adjective 'tiny'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumbleweed is a desert plant that breaks off and rolls in the wind, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Drab logic stifling on-line work

indicators.note: stifling means smothering and holding inside, so the letters lie concealed within drab logic

explanation.surface: Dull reasoning smothers someone's internet writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A weblog is a piece of writing posted on the internet, so on-line work describes it.

clue.text: Observant look about Catholic woman virtually in retreat

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the look word goes round the Catholic letters

parts.note: to peep is to take a quick look
RC stands for Roman Catholic

indicators.note: in retreat means going backwards, so the shortened name is read in reverse
virtually means almost all, so the woman's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Evita was the popular name for Eva Peron of Argentina

explanation.surface: A sharp-eyed glance at a Catholic woman almost in a religious retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' looks like a spiritual retreat; it reverses EVIT (EVITA trimmed by 'virtually') to TIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A perceptive person notices things quickly, a synonym for observant.

clue.text: On leaving Jobcentre, loses working experience of instructive nature

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked over into a new order
leaving means these letters depart from the word Jobcentre

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: Someone loses a working job after leaving a Jobcentre, a British state employment office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' is not ON but RE ('about'); removing RE from JOBCENTRE leaves JOBCENT, and 'working' shuffles that with LOSES.
explanation.definitionFit: An object lesson is a practical example that teaches a principle, an experience that instructs.

clue.text: One-time hits were played around back of hall

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters go round the letter from hall
played means performed in a new way, so hits were is rearranged
back of means the final letter of hall

explanation.surface: Old hit songs were performed around the rear of the concert hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Erstwhile means former, so it serves as a synonym for one-time in 'my one-time friend'.

clue.text: Ill-looking slum enemy laid waste with month gone

indicators.note: laid waste means wrecked, so the remaining letters are broken up and rearranged
gone means removed, so the month letter goes

explanation.surface: A slum is devastated by an enemy, with a month passing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word. Dropping M leaves SLUENEMY for 'laid waste' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Unseemly means improper or unbecoming, so ill-looking in its old sense of not decent in appearance.

clue.text: Custodian of pieces etc?

parts.note: pieces is slang for guns, so the keeper of a regiment's weapons is meant, not a museum curator

explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces' suggests chess or art; here pieces are firearms.
explanation.definitionFit: The armourer maintains and keeps weapons, so is a custodian of guns and similar kit.

clue.text: Windy condition captures one on edge by park, we hear

indicators.note: by means next to, so one piece follows the other

parts.note: on edge means tense, nervous

indicators.note: we hear signals the word for the park is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: a rec is a recreation ground, a public park

explanation.surface: Wind sweeps a park and catches somebody already jittery.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as someone gripped by a 'windy' (scared, British slang) state. 'Windy' looks like weather, not fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Windy is British slang for frightened; someone in the grip of that fearful state is a frazzled bag of nerves.

clue.text: Unstable snitch I found for nothing

indicators.note: found for means put in place of, so the letter is swapped in where the zero was

parts.note: to snitch is to inform on someone
O is the zero shape, nothing

explanation.surface: An unsteady informant: I discovered he got off free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I found for nothing' puts I in place of O in INFORM.
explanation.definitionFit: Infirm means weak and shaky in body, a synonym for unstable.

clue.text: Idiot eating fish producing dramatic comments

indicators.note: eating means taking inside, so the fish goes in the idiot word

parts.note: an ass is a fool
the ide is a freshwater fish, also called orfe

explanation.surface: A fool eating fish is a theatrical spectacle.
explanation.definitionFit: Asides are remarks an actor addresses to the audience, unheard by other characters on stage.

clue.text: Representative of ten characters in college

definitions.text: Representative of ten characters in college

parts.words: Representative of ten characters in college
parts.note: the ten letters E, F, G, H, I, J, K, L, M and N can be written as the span from ..., which names a famous school

explanation.surface: A school prefect stands for ten pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' are letters of the alphabet: from E to N there are exactly ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton is the famous English public school near Windsor, usually called Eton College.

clue.text: Criticise in work discontented trainees in casual gear

parts.note: to sweat is to work hard
to pan is to criticise harshly

indicators.note: discontented means emptied of contents, leaving only the outer letters of trainees

explanation.surface: Fed-up trainees at work are being told off, perhaps for their scruffy dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discontented' looks like 'unhappy' but means the middle is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose jogging trousers are informal clothing, an example of casual gear.

clue.text: Designate a place to park in announcement

indicators.note: in announcement says the words are spoken, so what is heard counts

parts.note: a lot is a car park, as in parking lot

explanation.surface: An announcement assigns someone a parking space.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to assign or allocate, a synonym for designate.

clue.text: A fool (not half) lifted cat

indicators.note: lifted means raised up, which in a down clue reads the letters bottom to top
not half means half of the fool word is removed

parts.note: a muppet is a fool

explanation.surface: A clown, half-hearted, raises a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' cuts MUPPET to MUP; A plus MUP is lifted to give the cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The puma, or cougar, is a large wild cat of the Americas.

clue.text: Moody scientist restricted in experimental realm

indicators.note: the cut-down scientist goes inside the rearranged letters
experimental means tried out in new forms, so realm is rearranged
restricted means cut short, so the scientist's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Marie Curie, the physicist and chemist

explanation.surface: A temperamental researcher is confined to a field of experiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'experimental' is the anagram signal for realm, and 'restricted' shortens Marie Curie's surname by its last letter before it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercurial describes someone whose mood changes quickly and unpredictably, a synonym for moody.

clue.text: Long narrative in detail I advanced

indicators.note: in signals the letters are found sitting within detail I advanced

explanation.surface: A long story in which the narrator has moved on into fine detail.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic poem about the Trojan War is a very long story in verse.

clue.text: Measure period for charge

parts.note: a yard is an imperial measure of length
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Sounds like an instruction to time a charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Yardage is a fee paid for using a yard or enclosure, for example to keep livestock.

clue.text: Article put on jolly huge drinks container

parts.note: the is the definite article
a Jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, RM
OS stands for outsize, very large

explanation.surface: Something placed on a big flask for drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' looks like 'cheerful'; in crosswords it is a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacuum flask that keeps drinks hot or cold is a kind of drinks container, by a trade name.
